---
title: OMK Graph
---

The primary data structure holding musical material is `OmkGraph`.

**Nodes** on an `OmkGraph` inherit from `OmkObject`, 
and represent anything you typically think of as *marks on a score* or discreet musical events.
Notes, rests, bar lines, time and key signatures, clefs, articulations, instrument designations,
lyrics, slurs, ties, phrase markings, chords, tempo markings, rehearsal numbers ---
these and many other things you might want to include in a score or piece of music
(including analysis and other "meta-musical" material) are nodes on the graph,
represented by instances of subclasses of `OMKObject`.

**Edges**, which connect nodes to each other and define their relationships,
are instances of subclasses of `OMKEdge`.
Edges can specify any type of relationship:
simultaneity, order, precedence, connection, attachment, inclusion, and many others.

::: {.callout-note}
We use the terms OmkGraph, OmkObject, and OmkEdge, 
rather than just "graph", "node", and "edge",
to indicate the logical/conceptual musical graph structure that OMK users interact with,
and to distinguish it from any underlying graph implementations used by OMK.
:::

## OmkObjects

::: {.callout-note}
The following is not an exhaustive list of all OmkObject types,
but a conceptual overview of the kinds of musical material that can be represented,
and how they are organized in the graph.
:::

### Structure and Musical Organization

An OMKGraph can have one or more Score nodes (or none),
which represent a distinct musical work or piece.

A Score node can connect to one or more Part nodes, 
which represent distinct musical parts or voices within that work.

Part nodes connect to the head node in a series of SequentialEvents,
which represent the musical material in the part, connected by a series of Next edges.

SequentialEvents include notes, rests, bar lines, time signatures, key signatures, clefs, and other musical material appearing in a line of music.
("Line" is not a formally defined term in OMK,
but is generally used to refer to a series of SequentialEvents connected by Next edges, which can be thought of as a musical line or voice.)
SequentialEvents carry a Duration (which will be ZeroDuration for things like bar lines, time signatures, and key signatures).
(OmkObjects which are not SequentialEvents, such as Score, Part, and Marking nodes, do not carry a Duration.)

Timing and cross-line simultaneity are calculated as needed
(usually at render time, whether that is to an engraved score, MusicXML, graph visualizer, MIDI, audio, or some analysis tool), 
by traversing the lines and summing Durations.
In the case of lines with disparate TemporalSystems, a TemporalRatio will need to be defined governing the relationship between the lines.

For convenience, and for the case of incomplete lines,
Simultaneous edges can be used to connect SequentialEvents across lines.
These is also a SyncLine construct, which can be used to connect simultaneous nodes across multiple lines
without having to connect each node to every other node in the simultaneity.
(This is never necessary, but can be convenient, especially for completed scores.
Graphs imported from MusicXML automatically create SyncLines and connect simultaneous bar lines to them.)

Bar lines and explicitly defined measures are optional.
Renderers can calculate measures based on the time signature and the durations of the notes and rests in a line.
(This is similar to LilyPond's approach, which does not require bar lines to be explicitly defined in the input.)
Additionally, there is no constraint that bar lines must create measures that match the time signature,
but renderers may raise errors or emit warnings if they encounter measures that do not match the time signature.

Lines can branch, using Branch edges to connect a SequentialEvent in a line to a SequentialEvent in a parallel line.

### Musical Material

A NoteEvent is a SequentialEvent that represents a note, group of simultaneous notes, or a rest.
It carries a collection of Tones and a Duration. (Rests are NoteEvents with a SilentTone.)

A ChordEvent is a SequentialEvent that represents a chord (such as in a lead sheet).
It carries a Chord and a Duration.
(Unlike many notation software systems, OMK does not require a ChordEvent to be connected to a NoteEvent;
a line of Chords is independent of any other line.)

NoteEvents and ChordEvents can be under-specified.
That is, they can carry a Duration without Tones or a Chord,
and they can carry Tones or a Chord without a Duration.
A missing Tone or Chord is not interpreted as a rest or unpitched sound, but is simply unspecified.
(Rests are specified with a SilentTone.)
A missing Duration is not interpreted as a ZeroDuration or unmetered duration, but is simply unspecified.
This allows for the representation of musical material that is incomplete or under-specified,
which can be useful in certain analytical or compositional contexts.

Time Signatures are represented by MeterEvent nodes,
which carry a Measurable TemporalElement such as a TimeSignature, or a similar construct in another TemporalSystem.
Key Signature are represented by ModalContextEvent nodes,
which carry a ModalContext such as a Key.

Markings, such as articulations, slurs, ties, phrase markings, dynamics, rehearsal numbers, and other performance or interpretive instructions,
are represented by a Marking node if they are attached to a single SequentialEvent,
or a MarkSpanner node if they are attached to a series of SequentialEvents.

Lyrics are represented by lines of LyricSyllable nodes,
which are a type of SequentialEvent (they can carry a Duration).
LyricSyllables can be connected to one or more NoteEvents or ChordEvents with `LYRIC` edges,
but this is not required, and a LyricSyllable can exist without being connected to any musical material.
(A set of lyrics, with no other musical material, is a valid OmkGraph or Score, 
as is a set of lyrics and chords alone.)
